title: Hobbies and free time
goal: Talk about what you like and enjoy, say how often you do things, and build sentences about actions.
bekal: say you like doing something with *uhibbu an*
say how often with frequency expressions
ask about other people's interests and respond

dialogs.title: حِوَار — مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ فِي عُطْلَةِ الْأُسْبُوعِ؟
dialogs.intro: Late afternoon in the campus garden, waiting for the rain to stop.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.text: مَاذَا تُحِبُّ أَنْ تَفْعَلَ فِي وَقْتِ فَرَاغِكَ؟
lines.baca: maadhaa tuhibbu an taf'ala fii waqti faraaghika?
lines.id: What do you like to do in your free time?
lines.literal: what you-like that you-do in time free-your?

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ وَأَنْ أَمْشِيَ فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ.
lines.baca: uhibbu an aqra'a wa an amshiya fil-hadiiqah.
lines.id: I like reading and walking in the park.
lines.literal: I-like that I-read and that I-walk in the-park.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: قِصَصًا قَصِيرَةً. وَأَحْيَانًا أُشَاهِدُ الْأَفْلَامَ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ.
lines.id: Short stories. And sometimes I watch Arabic films.
lines.literal: stories short. and sometimes I-watch the-films the-Arabic.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.id: Do you understand them without subtitles?

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: قَلِيلًا فَقَطْ. لٰكِنِّي أُحَاوِلُ كُلَّ أُسْبُوعٍ.
lines.baca: qaliilan faqaṭ. laakinnii uhaawilu kulla usbuu'.
lines.id: Only a little. But I try every week.
lines.literal: a-little only. but-I I-try every week.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.text: هٰذَا أَحْسَنُ طَرِيقَةٍ. وَهَلْ تُمَارِسُ الرِّيَاضَةَ؟
lines.baca: haadhaa ahsanu ṭariiqah. wa hal tumaarisur-riyaaḍah?
lines.id: That's the best way. Do you play sports?
lines.literal: this best way. and do you-practice the-sport?

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: نَعَمْ، أَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ.
lines.id: Yes, I play soccer twice a week.
lines.literal: yes, I-play ball the-foot twice in the-week.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.text: أَنَا لَا أُحِبُّ الرِّيَاضَةَ، أُفَضِّلُ الرَّسْمَ.
lines.id: I don't like sports, I prefer drawing.
lines.literal: I not I-like the-sport, I-prefer the-drawing.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.id: Really? Since when have you been drawing?

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.text: مُنْذُ الطُّفُولَةِ. أَرْسُمُ الْخَطَّ الْعَرَبِيَّ أَيْضًا.
lines.id: Since I was little. I also do Arabic calligraphy.
lines.literal: since the-childhood. I-draw the-calligraphy the-Arabic also.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَتَعَلَّمَ ذٰلِكَ! هَلْ تُعَلِّمِينَنِي؟
lines.baca: uriidu an ata'allama dhaalik! hal tu'allimiinanii?
lines.id: I'd love to learn that! Will you teach me?
lines.literal: I-want that I-learn it! will you-teach-me?

notes: **أَنْ + verb = "to do".** أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ ("I like to read"). Without أَنْ the sentence falls apart. أُحِبُّ الْقِرَاءَةَ ("I like reading") is also correct, but that is a noun, not an action.

**After أَنْ, the verb ending becomes fathah.** أَقْرَأُ → أَنْ أَقْرَأَ, أَمْشِي → أَنْ أَمْشِيَ, أَتَعَلَّمُ → أَنْ أَتَعَلَّمَ. This change is called *manṣub* (subjunctive), and it is triggered by أَنْ, لَنْ and لِ.

**Four verbs almost always followed by أَنْ:** أُحِبُّ أَنْ (like to), أُرِيدُ أَنْ (want to), أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ (can), يَجِبُ أَنْ (must). Learn these four and you've covered half of everyday conversation.

**كُرَةُ الْقَدَمِ — iḍafah again.** "Ball of the foot", i.e. football (soccer). Notice that in the sentence it becomes كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ because it is the object. Other sports: كُرَةُ السَّلَّةِ (basketball), كُرَةُ الطَّائِرَةِ (volleyball), تِنِس (tennis).
**مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ — saying how often.** The pattern: [how many times] + فِي + [unit of time]. مَرَّةً فِي الْيَوْمِ (once a day), ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ فِي الشَّهْرِ (three times a month).
**تُعَلِّمِينَنِي — two endings attached at once.** تُعَلِّمِينَ (you, f., teach) + نِي (me) = "you teach me". The ending ـنِي always means "me" as the object, unlike ـِي, which means "my".

**اَلْخَطُّ الْعَرَبِيُّ — calligraphy.** Literally "the Arabic line". Few topics warm an Arabic speaker's heart more than your interest in it, because it is seen as the height of the language's beauty.

grammars.title: أَنْ — linking two verbs

head: Arabic
Pronunciation
Meaning
rows: I hope to go to Egypt

after: The **first** verb changes with its subject as usual; the **second** verb changes for the same subject too, but its ending becomes fathah. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَذْهَبَ · تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَذْهَبَ · يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ.
To negate the future, use لَنْ, which works just like أَنْ: لَنْ أَذْهَبَ ("I won't go").

grammars.title: How often
after: أَبَدًا can't mean "never" on its own — it needs a negator: لَا أَشْرَبُ الْقَهْوَةَ أَبَدًا ("I never drink coffee"). On its own it actually means "forever".

blocks.text: Notice that almost all activity names are nouns with اَلْ, and most come from verbs you already know: قَرَأَ → اَلْقِرَاءَة, كَتَبَ → اَلْكِتَابَة, رَسَمَ → اَلرَّسْم, سَافَرَ → اَلسَّفَر. It's a very productive pattern — once you recognize it, you can form activity names from almost any verb yourself.

blocks.title: Two ways to say you like something
items: **أُحِبُّ الْقِرَاءَةَ** — "I like reading" (with a noun). Shorter and more common in conversation.
**أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ** — "I like to read" (with an action). Livelier, and required if you want to add details: أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ.
Both are correct. Practice them in turn so your ear gets used to the sound of أَنْ changing the verb ending.

head: Arabic
Pronunciation
Meaning
rows: What do you like to do?

blocks.text: One question that always opens a long conversation in the Arab world: هَلْ تُحِبُّ الْمُوسِيقَى الْعَرَبِيَّةَ؟ Music is as safe a topic as the weather, and almost everyone has strong opinions about it.

exercises.prompt: Join them with أَنْ. Watch the ending of the second verb.

items: I like to read short stories.
What do you like to do in your free time? (to a woman)
I play soccer twice a week.
I want to learn Arabic calligraphy.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the blanks with the right frequency word.
Write six sentences about your own hobbies, using أَنْ at least three times.
items: How often do you do it?
What would you like to learn?
What do you usually do on weekends?

answers: أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ — أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَذْهَبَ — أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ — يَجِبُ أَنْ نَدْرُسَ — تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَنَامَ — لَنْ أَرْجِعَ

أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ الْقِصَصَ الْقَصِيرَةَ. — مَاذَا تُحِبِّينَ أَنْ تَفْعَلِي فِي وَقْتِ فَرَاغِكِ؟ — أَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ. — لَا أَشْرَبُ الْقَهْوَةَ أَبَدًا. — أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَتَعَلَّمَ الْخَطَّ الْعَرَبِيَّ. — هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ تُسَاعِدَنِي؟
كُلَّ يَوْمٍ — أَحْيَانًا — أَبَدًا — نَادِرًا — دَائِمًا

Example: هِوَايَتِي اَلْقِرَاءَةُ — أَقْرَأُ مُنْذُ الطُّفُولَةِ — أَقْرَأُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ تَقْرِيبًا — أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَتَعَلَّمَ الرَّسْمَ أَيْضًا — لَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَلْعَبَ الرِّيَاضَةَ — فِي عُطْلَةِ الْأُسْبُوعِ أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَمْشِيَ فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ
